summaryBox.title: Aromaticity Criteria
summaryBox.takeaway: Aromatic: Cyclic, planar, conjugated, (4n+2) π e⁻ (Benzene, Tropylium C₇H₇⁺, Cyclopentadienyl anion). Anti-aromatic: 4n π e⁻ (Cyclobutadiene). Non-aromatic: COT (tub conformation).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
AROMATICITY COMPARISON MATRIX

• Aromatic Systems (Extraordinarily Stable): Cyclic, planar, conjugated with (4n+2) π-electrons.
  Examples: Benzene (6π e⁻, n=1), Tropylium cation (6π e⁻, n=1), Cyclopentadienyl anion (6π e⁻, n=1), Naphthalene (10π e⁻, n=2).
• Anti-Aromatic Systems (Extremely Unstable): Cyclic, planar, conjugated with 4n π-electrons.
  Example: Cyclobutadiene (4π e⁻, n=1).
• Non-Aromatic Systems: Non-cyclic OR non-planar.
  Example: Cyclooctatetraene (COT, 8π e⁻ adopts a non-planar Tub Conformation to avoid anti-aromaticity!).
conceptBreakdown.content: To achieve aromatic stabilization, a ring system must be cyclic, fully planar, continuously conjugated across $p$-orbitals, and contain $\mathbf{(4n+2)\ \pi\text{-electrons}}$ ($n = 0, 1, 2, \dots \implies 2, 6, 10, 14$).

conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 S_EAr Mechanism, Directing Effects, & The Halogen Anomaly
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
S_EAr PROFILES & HALOGEN ANOMALY

• Key Electrophiles:
  ├── Nitration: Nitronium Ion (NO₂⁺)
  ├── Sulfonation: Neutral Sulfur Trioxide (SO₃)
  ├── Halogenation: Halonium Ion (Cl⁺ / Br⁺)
  ├── FC Alkylation: Carbocation (R⁺, prone to 1,2-shifts!)
  └── FC Acylation: Acylium Ion (R-C⁺=O, NO shifts!)

• The Halogen Anomaly (F, Cl, Br, I):
  ├── Inductive Effect (-I > +M) ──► Deactivates the benzene ring (rate is slower than benzene!)
  └── Resonance Effect (+M)     ──► Directs incoming electrophile to Ortho and Para positions.
  Halogens are Ortho/Para-Directing BUT DEACTIVATING!
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Rate-Determining Step**: Attack of electrophile $\text{E}^+$ on benzene to form the non-aromatic **Arenium Ion / $\sigma$-Complex / Wheland Intermediate**.
• **Halogen Anomaly (CRITICAL NEST TRAP)**: Halogens are the only substituents that are **deactivating** (due to strong $-I$ effect) yet **ortho/para-directing** (due to $+M$ resonance stabilization of the $o,p$-arenium ion).

quickRevision: Tropylium cation (6π e⁻) and Cyclopentadienyl anion (6π e⁻) are aromatic.
COT assumes a non-planar tub shape and is non-aromatic.
Sulfonation uses neutral SO₃ as the electrophile.
